title: Reading — Words, Lines, a First Passage, and Timed Writing

lessons.title: (reading) — six words under one line
lessons.gloss: six words read cold — and the line across the top that holds them together

needs: your eyes, to read the printed text yourself
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your eyes, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want your eyes, to read the printed text yourself. The questions are about what you read, so save the whole lesson for when you have stopped.

segments.text: Every word below you have written. Not one is new.
What is new is that nobody says them first.
ভাত চা জল দুধ ভাই বোন.
Read down the list once, without stopping.
Again, and look at the top of each word rather than at the letters.
Bengali hangs its letters from a line instead of standing them on one. That line runs unbroken across a whole word and stops at its edge.
So the line is a word boundary you can see before you have read anything. A Bengali word looks like one object first and a row of signs second, which is the opposite of how you learned to write it.
ভাই and বোন are the shortest pair here and the easiest to tell apart at a glance, for exactly that reason.

segments.instruction: the six words down the list, once, without stopping
segments.source: [YOU SAY: the six words down the list, once, without stopping]

segments.text: How many of the six were new? (None.)
What shows you where a Bengali word ends? (The line stops.)

lessons.title: (reading) — six lines, and a bow nobody makes
lessons.gloss: six lines you would say to a stranger — and the one that is a whole sentence

needs: your eyes, to read the printed text yourself
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your eyes, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want your eyes, to read the printed text yourself. The questions are about what you read, so save the whole lesson for when you have stopped.

segments.text: The last lesson gave you words. These are things you would say.
You have said every one of them.
নমস্কার। ধন্যবাদ। হ্যাঁ। না। দয়া করে। স্বাগতম।.

segments.instruction: the six lines down once, without stopping
segments.source: [YOU READ: the six lines down once, without stopping]

segments.instruction: the six lines again, and notice the mark at the end of each line
segments.source: [YOU READ: the six lines again, and notice the mark at the end of each line]

segments.text: It is not a full stop but a দাঁড়ি, a single upright stroke.
নমস্কার is a bow written down: namas plus kara, the making of a bow. The commonest word in the language is a gesture that stopped being made.

দয়া করে is two words and means having done kindness. Bengali asks for things by describing what the other person has already generously done, which is a habit worth noticing on the page where it sits complete.
Six lines, and four of them are a single word.

segments.instruction: the six lines, once, in order, without stopping
segments.source: [YOU SAY: the six lines, once, in order, without stopping]

segments.prompt: Which line is the polite request?

segments.text: What ends a Bengali sentence? (A দাঁড়ি — one upright stroke.)
What is নমস্কার, literally? (The making of a bow.)

lessons.title: (reading) — the first passage
lessons.gloss: the first passage — thirty-six words of Bengali in a row, and not one of them new

needs: your eyes, to read the printed text yourself
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your eyes, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want your eyes, to read the printed text yourself. The questions are about what you read, so save the whole lesson for when you have stopped.

segments.text: Six words, then six lines. Now thirteen of them together.
Thirty-six words, and not one of them is new.
নমস্কার। আমার নাম রাম। আমি ভালো। এটা আমার ভাই। আমার পরিবার ভালো। আমি ভাত আর দুধ খাই। চা বা জল। আমি পড়ি। আমার বন্ধু এখানে। জামা লাল, কিন্তু কাপড় নীল। প্রথম আর দ্বিতীয়। হ্যাঁ, ভালো। ধন্যবাদ।.

segments.instruction: the passage once without stopping; do not translate as you go — let the sentences arrive
segments.source: [YOU READ: the passage once without stopping; do not translate as you go — let the sentences arrive]

segments.instruction: the passage again and find the three joining words
segments.source: [YOU READ: the passage again and find the three joining words]

segments.text: আর adds. বা offers a choice. কিন্তু turns the sentence.
Two of those are inherited and the third is not: কিন্তু came through Persian, which is why it does not sound like its neighbours. You can hear the borrowing without being told about it.
Notice also that the verb is last in every line that has one. আমি ভাত আর দুধ খাই — the eating comes after everything eaten, which is where Bengali always puts it.
This is the first whole passage the book has asked you to hold at once, and it works because everything in it was paid for.

segments.instruction: the passage aloud, once, without stopping
segments.source: [YOU SAY: the passage aloud, once, without stopping]

segments.text: Where does a Bengali verb go? (Last.)
Which of the three joiners is borrowed? (কিন্তু, through Persian.)

lessons.title: A short A1 writing checkpoint
lessons.gloss: a three-minute independent form attempt before the separate full A1 paper

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes or your hands for the steps that ask you to read, point, write or gesture
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes or your hands for the steps that ask you to read, point, write or gesture. You can listen to everything else now. I will say so again when we reach it, but leave this section until you have stopped: Warm-up.

segments.text: This is a short independent attempt, not a model. You will write the answers, and this page will not show you any copyable Bengali answer.

Put away romanization, dictionaries, translators, and spell-checkers. Keep a blank page ready and set a three-minute timer. Write in Bengali script. Ordinary legible handwriting is enough; decorative calligraphy is not scored.
One practical form — three minutes.

Complete all six fields in Bengali script for a new neighbourhood activity group. Short answers are enough. Start the timer when you begin the first field; leave any unfinished field as evidence when it rings.
Your name.
Where you live or stay.
A language you speak.
One everyday action or kind of work you do.
One drink or food you like.
One person in your family.
When the three-minute timer rings, stop. Record the number of completed fields. An honest short attempt is more useful than a perfect untimed one.
Spend at most one minute looking at this first attempt. Note one field you completed clearly and one field to practise next; do not rewrite the timed answer. Keep the page as evidence.

This checkpoint is not the complete A1 writing paper. On another day, close this lesson and open the separate A1 mock 1 learner paper for the authentic form and named-reader message under one 20-minute assessment clock. That paper and its later rubric review are a separate assessment session, not work inside this four-minute lesson. The second mock is a separate repeat, not a model to copy.
